data.coverAlt: A bound volume opened into separately tagged sections on a desk: knowledge units with rights, not one sealed blob.

title: A Document Has to Become a Knowledge Unit, Not a Blob
description: Today I persist VALESKA docs as section Knowledge Units, add a manual section hierarchy, and export a rights-tagged source slice. A blob with an embedding is not a unit of knowledge.
body:
A document that enters the index as one blob cannot be taught, cited, or licensed in pieces. Today I persist VALESKA docs as section Knowledge Units, add a section-hierarchy model for manual units, and export a rights-tagged source slice. I also stop using a busy embed as an excuse to fail the upsert: the conflict target is the SHA-256, and a busy embed is retried.

The wrong default

The usual ingest embeds the file and walks away. Later you cannot say which section a hit came from, whether that section was licensed for training, or whether two copies of the same bytes should have been one unit. I want a unit with a section, a hash, and a rights tag.

A textbook that can only be borrowed as a sealed brick cannot be assigned as a chapter. I am cutting chapters.

Units, hierarchy, rights

VALESKA’s own docs now persist as section Knowledge Units. The discovery model section_hierarchy_v1 lets me declare those sections by hand where the structure is known. The training export can take a rights-tagged slice of that source rather than a naked dump. Corpus characterization and a domain-discovery phase start the same day so I am not inventing the domain after the units exist.

A failed statement will no longer wedge every later memory write — that repair landed two days earlier, and it belongs with this operating week. pgAdmin is bound to localhost, with a healthcheck and a password file that actually persists. Those are how I stop the bench from leaking while I cut units. This is my documentation and my export. It is not a customer corpus already packed as Knowledge Units. It is my own data, cut into sections I can cite.

The upsert conflict target is the hash because two paths to the same bytes are one unit. A busy embed is a transient. Retrying it is cheaper than creating a second unit that will haunt retrieval. Rights tags on the export slice are how I refuse to train on a section I have not licensed to train on, including my own.

Manual section hierarchy is for the documents whose structure I already know. Automatic chunking remains for the rest. I will not pretend every PDF has been promoted to a Knowledge Unit today. The persist path exists. The hierarchy exists. The tagged slice exists.

pgAdmin on localhost only is the unglamorous half of the same week. A console that listens on the world while I cut units is how my own data leaves the machine without an ingest. A password file that does not persist is how the next restart invents a new secret and locks me out of the evidence I just wrote. One failed SQL statement wedging every later memory write is how a Knowledge Unit never lands. I fixed that first, then cut the units.

The next test

The next test is to retrieve a hit, name the section it came from, and show the rights tag on the exported slice. Until that is visible, this is a model and a persist path.

Historical basis: VALESKA commits e11a9ef, 2e7ced0, 43a1f0e, 16 August 2026; related ops fixes 14–15 August.
